title: Platform Critical Path Service Handbook
author: Maya Thompson
content:
Purpose

This handbook defines the canonical operational model for Redwood Inference platform services that sit on the critical path for customer-facing inference ("request intake -> routing -> serving runtime -> metrics/observability -> response delivery"). It consolidates: canonical inventory, ownership, SLOs, dashboard + alerting recipes, standard runbook playbooks, maintenance coordination steps, and retrospective triggers for continuous improvement.

Scope and audience

- Scope: services and system components that, if degraded, directly increase customer-visible latency, error rate, or cost per token. This includes API gateway, request router, model-serving clusters (pools), prefix/KV cache layer, billing-rate limiter, and primary observability pipelines.
- Audience: Platform engineers, SREs, on-call rotations, solutions engineers supporting Dedicated/Private customers, and product owners responsible for capacity and SLAs.

Executive summary

- Goal: keep end-to-end P99 latency below 450ms for API-hosted small-model baseline and maintain error-rate < 0.5% for production routes, with clear ownership and deterministic escalation.
- Primary levers: capacity routing policies, autoscaling thresholds, prefix cache hit-rate targets, fallback model variants, and automatic model-variant routing.

Service inventory (critical path)

The canonical inventory is authoritative for incident triage. Maintain this list in the platform team wiki and update on any ownership change.

Service | Primary owner | On-call rotation | SLO (user-visible)
API Gateway | api-platform | api-oncall | 99.9% availability, P99 latency < 100ms
Request Router | routing-service | routing-oncall | 99.95% availability, request routing < 20ms
Serving Pool (hosted-gpu) | runtime-sre | runtime-oncall | 99% availability, P99 token latency < 350ms
Prefix/KV Cache | cache-service | infra-oncall | cache-hit >= 80% for hot routes
Rate Limiter & Quota | billing-service | billing-oncall | throughput throttling < 0.1% of requests
Observability Pipeline | obs-platform | obs-oncall | metrics delivery < 30s, logs < 60s

(Above rendered as a Confluence table in product docs; keep single source of truth at sources/confluence/eng-platform/team-wiki/service-inventory-link)

SLOs, error budgets and burn policies

- User-visible SLOs (summary):
  - Availability: 99.9% for API gateway; 99% for serving pools.
  - Latency: P50/P90/P99 targets by model-size group; baseline small models P99 <= 450ms.
  - Error rate: overall 0.5% steady-state.
- Error budget policy: when a service consumes >25% of monthly error budget, ops review required; >50% triggers a platform freeze for non-urgent changes; >80% triggers an incident response and executive notification.

Dashboard and alerting cookbook

Minimum dashboards (per-service): Overview, Critical-Path Latency Breakdown, Consumer-Impact (routes), Capacity & Utilization, Cache Behavior, Cost/Token trend.

Suggested Grafana panels and Prometheus rules (examples):

1) P99 latency panel query (PromQL):
  histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="api-gateway"}[5m])) by (le))

2) Alert: P99 latency breach (5m sustained)
  ALERT: APIGateway_P99_Latency_High
  IF histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="api-gateway"}[5m])) by (le)) > 0.1
  FOR 5m
  LABELS { severity = "page" }
  ANNOTATIONS { summary = "API Gateway P99 latency > 100ms" }

3) Alert: Cache hit-rate drop
  ALERT: PrefixCache_Hit_Rate_Low
  IF (sum(rate(cache_hits_total[5m])) / sum(rate(cache_requests_total[5m]))) < 0.75
  FOR 10m
  LABELS { severity = "high" }
  ANNOTATIONS { summary = "Prefix/KV cache hit rate below 75%" }

Escalation and paging policy (short form)

1) Pager: Severity = page -> page primary oncall for implicated service and routing-oncall.
2) War room: If cross-service impact or error budget > 50%, escalate to platform lead and SRE manager; create incident channel (#inc-<id>).
3) Exec notify: If customer SLA risk or >80% budget burn, open exec brief.

Playbooks (runbooks)

Runbook: High P99 latency impacting customers
1) Triage: identify affected routes via Critical-Path Latency Breakdown dashboard. Note correlated metrics: CPU/GPU utilization, queue length, cache hit-rate, request fan-out.
2) Narrow scope: check routing logs to determine if a model variant change, autoscale event, or fulldisk/oom occurred.
3) Quick mitigations (ordered by impact-risk):
   a) Activate routing fallback to smaller model variant for impacted routes (use routing-control API):
      curl -X POST https://platform-internal/api/v1/routing/fallback \
        -H 'Authorization: Bearer $PLATFORM_TOKEN' \
        -d '{"route": "customer-A/encode", "fallback_variant": "quantized-8bit"}'
   b) Increase serving pool target count by +30% (scale-out via autoscaler override) for 15m.
   c) Temporarily raise prefix cache TTL for hot keys to improve hit-rate.
4) Post-incident: open a retrospective and follow RCA template (see below).

Runbook: Observability pipeline lag / missing metrics
1) Validate Prometheus and metrics-forwarder service health.
2) If metrics backlog > 10m, increase consumer replicas and replay backlog (obs-tool replay --from <timestamp>).
3) If logs are delayed, toggle high-priority sampling to ensure root-cause traces are retained.

Maintenance coordination and safe-deploy checklist

Purpose: prevent maintenance windows from cascading into platform-wide latency spikes.

Before maintenance (48–72h):
- Announce in #platform-announce and schedule via maintenance calendar.
- Validate canary plan: 1% traffic route to target, 5m observation, then 10% over 30m.
- Confirm rollback playbook and automatic fallback policy are enabled.
- Ensure oncall coverage and page routing for changes.

During maintenance:
- Monitor Critical-Path Latency dashboard and error budget burn in real-time.
- Hold release cadence to per-10% increments only if metrics remain green.

Rollback procedure (emergency):
1) Execute automated routing rollback: POST /api/v1/routing/rollbacks with previous commit id.
2) If rollback fails, manually switch to fallback model variant and scale serving pool back to stable commit.
3) If traffic still fails, temporarily divert traffic to a regional backup endpoint (see routing-control playbook).

Troubleshooting checklist (quick reference)

- Are the API gateway and request router healthy? (check /health endpoints and last 5m error rate)
- Has a new model variant been rolled out recently? (check rollout history and leader election logs)
- Is cache hit-rate degraded? (cache-metrics page)
- Is GPU/worker queue length unusually high? (serving-pool utilization)
- Any unusual billing spikes affecting rate limiter? (billing-metrics)
- Observability lag? (metrics/trace pipeline)

Retrospective triggers and template

Trigger a blameless retrospective when:
- Any outage > 15m that caused customer-visible errors,
- Error budget consumed > 50% in a 7-day window, or
- Repeated alert flapping across the same service within 72h.

Retrospective template (to be completed within 72h):
1) Timeline of events (who, what, when).
2) Root cause analysis (technical + process).
3) Immediate mitigations and why they worked/didn't.
4) Action items (owner, ETA, verification method).
5) Dashboard and alert tuning changes (if any).

Example action item table (text form):
- Action: Increase prefix cache default TTL for session-based keys. Owner: cache-service team. ETA: 2026-02-15. Verification: cache-hit-rate >= 80% for two weeks.

Platform roadmap items (next 6 months)

- Phase 1 (Q1): Standardize critical-path dashboards and publish per-route SLOs; implement automatic fallback for top-10 customer routes.
- Phase 2 (Q2): Add adaptive autoscaling for serving pools based on per-route sequence-length predictions.
- Phase 3 (Q3): Deliver cost-aware routing policy that optimizes for cost-per-token with controlled latency impact.

  platformctl routing get --route customer-A/encode

  # set fallback variant for route
  platformctl routing set-fallback --route customer-A/encode --variant quantized-8bit --expires 900
